# Aluminium PFC {#sec-aluminum}

`apps/aluminumNew` — a compact PFC application in the same family as
@sec-tungsten, parameterised for aluminium and built around a moving frame.

## Physical setting

The same phase-field crystal picture as @sec-tungsten: a conserved periodic
density whose minima are lattice sites. The differences are the equation of
state, an FCC seeding initial condition (`seed_grid_fcc`), and a moving-frame
formulation aimed at directional solidification, where the interesting physics
is a front travelling through the domain rather than a bulk relaxation.

The question the application is built to answer is the directional-solidification
one: **pull a temperature gradient through an aluminium melt at a fixed speed —
where does the front settle, and what grain structure does it leave behind?**
The observable is again the front position, together with the per-cell free
energy this application computes and the field checksums.

That said, the shipped configuration does **not** ask that question. Both
`aluminumNew.json` and `inputs_json/smoke.json` set
$G_{\mathrm{grid}} = V_{\mathrm{grid}} = 0$, which switches the thermal drive
off entirely and leaves an isothermal run. The moving-frame machinery described
below is present and tested, but no shipped preset exercises it.

## Problem setup

Two inputs ship. `aluminumNew.json` is a large demonstration case;
`inputs_json/smoke.json` is a $16^3$ sanity file that is not referenced by
CMake or by any test. Neither is a verification preset: the pinned checksum in
the test suite runs a **separate synthetic $32^3$ configuration built in C++**
(`X0 = 8`, radius 4, `rseed = 42`), not either of these files.

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Use case | An aluminium melt with a row of FCC seeds, intended for directional solidification; as shipped, an isothermal seeded-growth run |
| Domain | $1024 \times 2048 \times 256$ cells at $\Delta x = 2\pi\sqrt3/8 \approx 1.3603$, i.e. $1393 \times 2786 \times 348$ in reduced PFC length units, origin at the corner. Eight cells per FCC lattice constant ($a = 2\pi\sqrt3$ with the peak at $\lvert\mathbf{k}\rvert = 1$) |
| Grid | $t \in [0, 2000]$ at $\Delta t = 1$ (2000 steps), field dump every 200 |
| Boundary conditions | Periodic on all three axes (the FFT has no other mode), plus a stationary `fixed` density-reservoir band pulling $\psi$ between $-1.297$ and $-0.006$ near the high-$x$ end |
| Initial condition | Uniform $\psi = -0.006$, then `seed_grid_fcc`: a $2 \times 1$ row of FCC seeds of radius 120 at $x = 130$, amplitude $0.4$, $\rho = -0.036$, each jittered by $\pm 0.2R$ and randomly oriented. Each seed is built from the four $\langle 111\rangle$ wave vectors, in contrast to @sec-tungsten's six $\{110\}$ vectors |
| Key physical parameters | $T_{\mathrm{const}} = 980$, $T_0 = 89285$ (no unit is stated anywhere in this application, unlike @sec-tungsten's TOML comments); $n_{\mathrm{sol}} = -0.036$, $n_{\mathrm{vap}} = -1.297$; $B_x = 0.8179$, $\alpha = 0.20$; barred polynomial coefficients. $G_{\mathrm{grid}} = V_{\mathrm{grid}} = 0$: **the shipped run is isothermal**. Lengths and times are reduced PFC units with no SI mapping in the repository |
| Observable | `SPECTRAL_CHECKSUM` sum, sum of squares and $L^2$ of $\psi$; the summed free energy (`last_free_energy_sum`), which this application computes per cell and @sec-tungsten does not; binary field dumps |
| Model maturity | numerical verification: **regression** — the operators and the pointwise nonlinearity are checked to $10^{-14}$ against an independently written reference formula, and one synthetic case is pinned; there is no closed-form solution of the model · physical completeness: **extended** — the tungsten equation of state plus a separate correlation kernel $P(k)$ and a travelling temperature field · calibration: **representative**, with the same caveat as @sec-tungsten: no source is cited anywhere in the repository for any of the aluminium coefficients |

Periodicity plus the reservoir band means the same thing here as in
@sec-tungsten: a melt column that the solid can grow into, with no free
surface, no crucible and no container wall. What is specific to this
application is the $x$ direction. The domain is deliberately long and thin
($1024 \times 2048$ cells in the plane), which is the geometry of a
directional-solidification cell rather than a bulk sample, and the front is
tracked along $x$ with the temperature field unwrapped relative to it. Nothing
in the model represents convection in the melt, solute partitioning, or a
second chemical component.

## Governing equations

Conserved PFC dynamics, as in @eq-w-dyn:

$$
\partial_t \psi \;=\; \nabla^2 \frac{\delta F}{\delta \psi}.
$$

The free energy has the same structure as @eq-w-energy — a quadratic
correlation term plus a local polynomial in $\psi$ and the mean-field density
— with the aluminium coefficients $\bar p_2,\bar p_3,\bar p_4$ and
$\bar q_{20},\dots,\bar q_{40}$.

## Spectral formulation

$$
L(k) \;=\; u\,C(k), \qquad M_{\mathrm{nl}}(k) \;=\; u ,
\qquad u = k_{\mathrm{lap}} = -|\mathbf{k}|^2 .
$$ {#eq-al-symbol}

Alongside $C(k)$ the model carries a separate **correlation kernel** $P(k)$
applied to the density each step. The pointwise nonlinearity is therefore a
function of four arguments rather than two,

$$
N \;=\; N\big(\psi,\ \psi_{\mathrm{MF}},\ (P*\psi),\ T_{\mathrm{var}}(x,t)\big),
$$ {#eq-al-nl}

where $(P*\psi)$ is the kernel-filtered density — a convolution in real space,
hence a multiply in reciprocal space — and $T_{\mathrm{var}}$ is the imposed
temperature field.

## Moving frame and thermal drive

The temperature *departure* from the base value varies in space and time as a
travelling profile,

$$
T_{\mathrm{var}}(x,t) \;=\;
  G_{\mathrm{grid}}\big(\tilde x - x_{\mathrm{initial}} - V_{\mathrm{grid}}\,t\big),
$$ {#eq-al-temp}

where $\tilde x$ is the $x$ coordinate unwrapped relative to the tracked front
position, so the profile follows the front around the periodic box rather than
jumping when it wraps. The pointwise nonlinearity then uses
$T_{\mathrm{const}} + T_{\mathrm{var}}$, not $T_0 + T_{\mathrm{var}}$: $T_0$
is the reference temperature that the ratio $T/T_0$ is formed against, not an
offset.

A gradient $G_{\mathrm{grid}}$ pulled through the domain at speed
$V_{\mathrm{grid}}$ is the standard directional-solidification setup: the front
settles where the local temperature matches the interface condition, and then
travels with the gradient. Setting $G_{\mathrm{grid}} = 0$ — the shipped value
— recovers an isothermal run at `T_const`.

::: {.callout-warning}
## `T_min` and `T_max` do nothing

The schema declares `T_min` and `T_max` as required parameters and every
shipped input and test supplies them, but **no code reads them**. There is no
clamping of the temperature field anywhere in the application. They are
vestigial, and a reader should not assume the travelling profile is bounded.
:::

## Solution strategy

ETD1 as in @eq-etd1, with the mean-field filter and the correlation kernel
evaluated as reciprocal-space multiplies. Two transforms per step plus the
kernel application.

As in @sec-tungsten, **dealiasing is off**: the shared option defaults to
`false` and this application never enables it.

## Verification

* **Reference-formula agreement.** The mean-field filter, the correlation
  kernel, the linear symbol, the nonlinearity and the free-energy density all
  match an independently written reference formula to $10^{-14}$. This is the
  strongest check the application has, and it is a code-to-code equivalence,
  not a closed-form solution.
* **Pinned checksum.** One literal is pinned, for a synthetic $32^3$
  five-step `seed_grid_fcc` case built in the test — **not** for either shipped
  input file.
* **CPU/GPU parity.** A live CPU run and a live device run agree to $10^{-10}$.
  There is no separately pinned GPU literal.
* **Schema.** JSON round-trip and range validation on every parameter.

Like @sec-tungsten this model has no closed-form reference; coverage is
regression and schema rather than analytical.

## Binaries and inputs

`aluminum_etd` (CPU), `aluminum_etd_cuda`, `aluminum_etd_hip`. Preset
`inputs_json/smoke.json`, plus `aluminumNew.json`.

## Scalability

Not measured. The application shares the spectral ETD stack with
@sec-tungsten, so its per-step cost is expected to track the tungsten curve at
equal grid size, but that has not been verified and no curve is reported here.
